messages:
sara: Heads up — hosted API p99 spiked around 17:04 UTC, p95 drifting too. Dashboard shows a short plateau then large tail. https://dash.redwood/hosted/api
james: Can you paste tenant id or some request ids? I’ll pull traces.
sara: tenant-42 (internal tid-42). correlates with a fanout-heavy job from their app.
ops-bot: alert: hosted-api-p99 2026-03-18T17:04:00Z -> 17:08:00Z (+420ms)
maria: quick profiler dump: looks like kernel selector flipped to `aux` for ~12/18 affected shards after the autoscaler bounce. That kernel is slower for short sequences.
ken: I see kselector toggles in pod logs. snippet: ```
[2026-03-18T17:04:12Z] kselector: chosen=aux kernel_id=3 seq_len_bucket=8
[2026-03-18T17:04:12Z] kernel_init: runtime_ms=1.8
```
james: KV cache hit-rate dropped on those shards: `kv_hit_ratio=0.62` (baseline ~0.88). Eviction rate spiked.
sara: batching sampler telemetry shows median batch_size fell from 2.8 -> 1.3 in the window, so more single-request small batches increasing per-token overhead.
maria: perf top snapshot indicates kernel stalls and increased warp divergence on aux kernel for short seqs — matches batch size shrink.
ken: noisy tenant detail: tenant-42 burst ~18k short completions in 4m; many function-calls => small tokens, lots of KV churn. Rate limiter started queueing near 850 rps.
james: plausible root causes: (A) kernel selector heuristic misclassified short, fanout-heavy workload to aux; (B) kv cache thrash due to many unique keys from function calls; (C) batching sampler reacted to queue patterns producing smaller batches.
sara: mitigation steps I want to try now: override kselector -> primary on affected pods; bump local KV cache mem-capacity on those pods; apply soft tenant throttling for tenant-42.
dev-bot: rollout: kselector-override primary applied to 6 pods (pods: rtd-ker-10..15) — started 2026-03-18T17:06:02Z.
ken: applied kv cache size increase to same pods at 17:06:45Z.
ops-bot: noted temporary tenant throttle of tenant-42 at 17:07:10Z (rate cap 600rps).
sara: after overrides, p99 dropped ~250ms within 90s, p95 back to normal. KV hit ratio recovering to 0.81 within 3m.
maria: interim conclusion: kselector flip + KV thrash + smaller batches amplified GPU kernel inefficiency -> latency spike.
james: action items: 1) add a safety rule in kselector: avoid aux for seq_len < 16 when fanout/func-call rate > threshold; 2) add kv prefetch/warm path for detected fanout patterns; 3) collect richer batch-size distribution telemetry around selector decisions.
ken: assigning eng-runtime + eng-ml owners to prototype heuristic changes and a canary.
sara: please open incidents/pm with timeline and attach logs/traces. I'll paste the postmortem link here when ready. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0318-042.
james: I'll open a small PR with telemetry first, then canary rollout plan.
maria: will follow up with kernel optimization notes — may be a low-hanging perf win if we avoid aux for short sequences.
sara: thanks team, great quick cleanup. Closing this thread — will update with postmortem link.
